# The tectonic timeout corpus (64-05)

Generated by `scripts/cmd/gen-tectonic-corpus.py`, committed so the measurement
behind `TECTONIC_ENGINE_TIMEOUT` is reproducible by anyone and re-runnable when
the bundle or the engine changes.

Every document uses **only packages from `convert.TeXPackages`**. A corpus that
needed a package the bundle lacks would measure the admission gate rather than
the engine.

## Three classes, by how many passes the document forces

The class axis is the point. Tectonic reruns the TeX engine until its references
converge, so cost is per **pass**, and a corpus of single-pass documents would
measure the wrong thing confidently — which is what `.env.example` said about
this number for as long as it was a placeholder.

| class | what forces the passes | passes observed |
|---|---|---|
| `single` | nothing — no `\label`/`\ref`, no toc, no bibliography | 2 |
| `xref` | `\tableofcontents` + forward `\ref`/`\eqref` | 3 |
| `bib` | `biblatex` with `backend=bibtex` (D-07: no biber) | 7 |

Seven is not a corpus statistic — it is the **engine's own ceiling**. Tectonic
says so itself: `warning: TeX rerun seems needed, but stopping at 6 passes`.
Every `bib` document hits it, at every size.

Note that even `single` costs **two** passes: tectonic runs once more to confirm
the output is stable. There is no such thing as a one-pass job here.

## Four sizes, and why `xl` exists

`s`/`m`/`l` are 2/20/60 sections. `xl` is 220.

`xl` was added after the first measurement run: at `s`/`m`/`l` the per-page term
was entirely inside the noise — `single-l` (30 pages) timed *faster* than
`single-s` (1 page). A per-page cost that cannot be separated from jitter is not
a measurement, and the harness now also runs each file three times and keeps the
slowest.

## The ceiling document is NOT committed

`bib-bound.tex` — 1280 sections, 2 143 444 bytes, 745 pages — is the document
the shipped number is actually derived from, because a bound extrapolated to its
ceiling is not measured at it. Note it is 2.2% LARGER than the 2 097 152-byte
input ceiling the API enforces, so the timeout covers slightly more work than
the service will accept. Found by POSTing this very file to the live API after
the ceiling shipped and watching it come back 413.

It is regenerated on demand rather than committed, since two 2 MiB files would
outweigh everything else in `testdata` combined:

```
python3 scripts/cmd/gen-tectonic-corpus.py <dir> --bound
```

The generator is deterministic, so the file is byte-identical on every run.

## Measured (2026-09-04, `octoconv-tectonic-worker`, tectonic 0.17.0, 2 CPU / 1 GiB, `--network none`, `USER nobody`)

| document | bytes | pages | passes | seconds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `single-xl` | 345 376 | 110 | 2 | 1.021 |
| `xref-xl` | 363 686 | 127 | 3 | 2.851 |
| `bib-xl` | 368 999 | 129 | 7 | 44.189 |
| `bib-bound` (1 MiB variant) | 1 071 659 | 373 | 7 | 90.0 |
| `bib-bound` (2 MiB) | 2 143 444 | 745 | 7 | **180.3** |

Cost is linear in source size within the `bib` class: 1 MiB → 90.0s,
2 MiB → 180.3s. The full pipeline (S3 download + engine + upload, measured
through the live API on the same 2 MiB document) took 184.9s — the engine is
97.5% of the job.

Full output: `.planning/phases/64-tectonic-ninth-engine-class/evidence/`.
